subject: NovaPayments production: latency & 5xx spike — hot-key mitigation playbook and exec sync
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@novapay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production latency + 5xx spike affecting /payments - urgent

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a significant regression on the Redwood-powered /payments endpoint around 08:50 PDT. Symptoms: p95 latency climbed from ~450ms to ~3.8s, p99 to ~8s, and overall 5xx error rate across the fleet rose to ~4%. Throughput (rps) dropped ~22% as client-side timeouts kicked in.

We pulled a few request IDs and attached a short log dump (novapay-prod-logs-20270726.txt). This is directly impacting settlement windows for our merchants — we need an urgent mitigation and a short timeline for a fix.

What we need from Redwood: immediate mitigation (any toggle / config to reduce errors), and an ETA for a durable fix. We are open to a temporary routing change or throttling on our side if that helps.

Please escalate.

— Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform, NovaPayments
elaine@novapay.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-26T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike affecting /payments - urgent

Team — escalating. NovaPayments reporting a hard regression (p95/p99 up, spikes in 5xx, throughput drop). Attached logs show repeated long tail KV hits for a small set of customer keys; initial hypothesis is hot-key-induced HOL blocking and eviction thrash in our KV cache tier.

Immediate ask (please action now):
- Marcus: run emergency mitigation steps (list below). Report back metrics T+5/15/30 minutes.
- Grace: start a quick triage to confirm whether recent kv-config changes (eviction_policy/entry_size_limit) or a model rollout correlate.
- Neha: loop in CS for an exec-level customer update and surface any ask for credits/SLA responses.

Emergency mitigation checklist (do not wait for full triage):
1) Temporarily increase hot-lane capacity for NovaPayments tenant (hot_lane_slots += 4).
2) Reduce max batch window for endpoints touching heavy keys (20ms -> 5ms) to reduce HOL blocking.
3) Increase per-key cache allocation (max_entries_per_key +50%).
4) Disable aggressive prefix prefetch for NovaPayments to avoid speculative thrash.
5) If error rates persist, shift NovaPayments traffic to an alternate compatible model variant with smaller attention footprint.

I attached their logs and a kv-stats snapshot. Marcus — please paste the commands you run into the thread. We need clear timestamps for customer communication.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-26T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike affecting /payments - urgent

On 2027-07-26 09:20, Kimberly Park wrote:
> Team — escalating. NovaPayments reporting a hard regression ... initial hypothesis is hot-key-induced HOL blocking and eviction thrash in our KV cache tier.

Actions taken (now):
- Increased hot lane slots for tenant nova_payments (was 2 -> set to 6). Command: `redwood-admin tenant update --id nova_payments --hot-lane-slots 6`
- Reduced batch coalescing window for payment path: `redwood-admin path config set /payments --batch-window-ms 5`
- Raised per-key cache soft limit for tenant by 50%: `redwood-kv set-tenant-quota nova_payments --per-key-entries 1500`
- Disabled prefix prefetch for tenant: `redwood-kv set-prefetch nova_payments --enabled false`
- Rolled traffic to compatible smaller-parameter variant (rwd-gpt-3.4-compact) for affected routes as fallback.

Immediate observations (T+7m):
- p95 for /payments from 3.8s -> ~1.1s
- p99 from ~8s -> ~2.6s
- 5xx rate from ~4% -> 0.7%
- Throughput recovered ~14% (still below baseline)

I left KV eviction policy as-is for now to avoid mass thrash during change; once stable we can tune eviction thresholds. I also captured a kv-stats snapshot (attached).

Will keep monitoring; sending metrics dashboards to this thread.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-26T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike affecting /payments - urgent

Good notes — quick analysis from the runtime traces:
- Root cause: small set of tenant keys ~10 keys showed disproportionate size and access freq. Large KV values caused long deserialization + memory pinning on the hot lane, producing HOL blocking for in-flight batches.
- Secondary effect: aggressive prefix prefetch (recently enabled per-tenant optimization) caused many speculative entries to populate the cache, triggering eviction churn and repeated remote fetches (thrash).

Medium-term remediation plan (1–3 days):
1) Per-tenant key sharding: split large logical keys into multiple subkeys for NovaPayments (low-friction change we can push as config).
2) Introduce per-key LRU with soft TTL for large entries (>32KB).
3) Add a hot-key breaker: when a single key exceeds X ops/s or average fetch time > Y ms, divert to dedicated hot-lane instances with larger KV allotment.
4) Rework prefix prefetch heuristics to respect a size/access-frequency budget.

Customer communication: recommend scheduling a 30-min technical sync with NovaPayments ops in next 2 hours to walk through immediate mitigations and share the 72-hour plan. I prepared a short mitigation checklist and a doc (nova-mitigation-checklist.md) — link in this thread.

I'll own follow-up instrumentation work and a regression test to catch this pattern in CI.

-Grace
Grace O'Connor
Principal Applied Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-26T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary for leadership: NovaPayments outage + proposed remediation and customer ask

Neha — short executive summary to share with the leadership channel and NovaPayments execs: please review and advise on credits/PR wording.

What happened:
- Customer NovaPayments experienced a production regression (latency p95/p99 and 5xx spike) starting 08:50 PDT driven by a hot-key pattern + prefix-prefetch-induced KV eviction thrash.

Immediate impact and mitigations applied (completed within 20 minutes):
- Increased hot-lane capacity and per-key cache allotment for the tenant.
- Reduced batch window to lower HOL blocking.
- Disabled aggressive prefix prefetch and rolled traffic to a smaller model variant as fallback.
- Observed p95 improved from ~3.8s -> ~1.1s and 5xx reduced to ~0.7% at T+20m.

Proposed next steps (72-hour plan):
- Apply per-key sharding and per-key LRU/soft TTL for large entries.
- Implement hot-key breaker to automatically divert to dedicated hot-lane resources.
- Tune prefetch heuristics and add regression tests for hot-key patterns.

Customer ask (NovaPayments):
- Exec-level update and short-term financial remediation (requesting consideration for a credit for impacted settlement window).

Recommendation for leadership:
- Approve a one-off service credit (up to one week of hosted fees) pending CS negotiation.
- Approve a customer-facing postmortem once we have full RCA (~72h).
- Prioritize implementation of hot-key breaker and prefetch budget in the performance backlog (P1 for Dedicated ops).

If OK I will send a calibrated note to NovaPayments (ops + exec) with the timeline and offer a technical sync in the next 2 hours.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
